advances: An exact all-ambient-normal value on the six-fiber area product, with uniqueness on each middle fiber.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ for barycentric coordinates in $T$. At any mark $(j,x)$ take a coordinate $\lambda_i(x)\ge1/3$ and a cap whose own trace is $\lambda_i\ge\lambda_i(x)$. This triangle has area $(1-\lambda_i(x))^2\le4/9$. A sufficiently large finite base tilt captures exactly that trace and all the whole fibers on a chosen side of $j$. Choose the side with fewer bases. The upper bounds at the outer pair, the next pair, and the middle pair of bases are respectively $4/9,13/9,22/9$. If $x\ne g$ on either middle fiber some $\lambda_i(x)>1/3$ and the last bound is strict.

It remains to prove the lower bound at $(0,g)$, as the reflection $z\mapsto1-z$ then gives the other one. A containing halfspace can be tightened through the mark. A pure-base through-cap has at least three full fibers, including the boundary fiber. For every nonzero continuous normal, center its continuous functional at $g$, order its values at the vertices, and divide by minus its lowest value. The three values sum to zero and have positive range, so the ordered normalized heights are $-1,t,1-t$ with $-1\le t\le1/2$. For $-1<t<1/2$ the upper cap-area fraction is
$$
F_t(s)=
\begin{cases}
1 & s\le-1,\\
1-(s+1)^2/[(t+1)(2-t)] & -1\le s\le t,\\
(1-t-s)^2/[(2-t)(1-2t)] & t\le s\le1-t,\\
0 & s\ge1-t.
\end{cases}
$$
The middle formulas follow from the products of the two edge fractions of the removed or retained corner. The branch values agree at common endpoints. Closed cut lines have zero area. With real normalized tilt $L$, the raw mass is $G(t,L)=\sum_{k=-2}^3 F_t(kL)$. The five terms at $-2,\ldots,2$ are unchanged as a sum when $L$ is reversed, and for negative $L$ the remaining term $F_t(3L)$ is no smaller than $F_t(3|L|)$. It suffices to consider $L\ge0$. For $L\ge2$, $G=2+F_t(0)\ge22/9$. For $-1<t\le0$ this last bound follows by subtracting $4/9$ from the upper-branch formula: the numerator with denominator $9(2-t)(1-2t)$ is $(t+1)^2$. For $0\le t<1/2$, the lower-branch formula gives $F_t(0)\ge1/2$ since $(t+1)(2-t)\ge2$.

For $0\le L\le2$ let $D=(t+1)(2-t)(1-2t)$ and $P=9DG-22D$. Use the [rational certificate](../assets/pk-nov6/computations/triangle-six-fiber-depth-bernstein-certificate.json), SHA-256 16dcbe6a1852a1a52e6208f9096cf67b1d76d7da85a2e884377f8f841d67ac82, also printed as triangles and coefficients in the source Appendix A. Its 22 convex polygon cells lie in the rectangle $[-1,1/2]\times[0,2]$. The signs of $kL+1$, $kL-t$, and $kL-(1-t)$ on their vertices determine a common branch for each summand on each cell, including $k=0$. The full, lower, upper and empty contributions to $DG$ are respectively $D$, $D-(kL+1)^2(1-2t)$, $(1-t-kL)^2(t+1)$, and zero. Thus $P$ is a specified cubic on each cell.

For a listed triangle with vertices $A,B,C$, substitute $(t,L)=A+u(B-A)+v(C-A)$. If the resulting cubic is $\sum p_{ab}u^av^b$, its coefficient at the degree-three Bernstein basis element indexed by $i,j$ is
$$
b_{ij}=\sum_{a\le i,\ b\le j}p_{ab}\,
\frac{\binom ia\binom jb}{\binom3{a+b}\binom{a+b}a}.
$$
Expanding the monomial $u^av^b$ using $(u+v+(1-u-v))^{3-a-b}$ proves this formula in the basis $3!u^iv^j(1-u-v)^{3-i-j}/[i!j!(3-i-j)!]$. All basis elements are nonnegative on the triangle. The rational data give 380 nonnegative recomputed coefficients on 38 triangles. The triangles are contained in their stated cells, have pairwise intersection of area zero there, and their areas sum to each cell's area. The cells have pairwise intersection of area zero and sum to area three, the rectangle's area. These arithmetic assertions, including the branch inequalities and each coefficient, are checked by the [Fraction-only verifier](../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_triangle_six_depth_bernstein_certificate.py), SHA-256 272b687ad8c4921223ea86d3e36ae0ee6701d8fd37627ab3a3b1ea450ef97985. Both unions are finite and closed, so a missing point would give positive omitted relative area, proving coverage. Thus $P\ge0$ and, since $D>0$ in the open $t$ strip, $G\ge22/9$ there.

For $t=-1,1/2$ take normalized affine functionals with nearby distinct vertex heights and keep $L$ fixed. Their coefficients converge since vertex values do, and the limiting continuous linear part is nonzero, so every limiting cut line has zero area. Dominated convergence proves the same inequalities for the repeated-height endpoints. This handles all normals and proves the assertion by the preceding upper bounds.

statement: Let $T\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a triangle of area one and centroid $g$. For $[-2,3]\times T$ use the measure summing areas at its six consecutive integer bases. The exact maximum raw closed-halfspace depth is $22/9$, attained only at $(0,g)$ and $(1,g)$. The maximum normalized depth is $11/27$.
title: Exact all-normal depth of the six-identical-triangle interval
